what: Synaptics designs chips that connect people to devices: touch and display controllers, wireless connectivity chips (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, GPS), and processors for smart home, industrial and automotive devices. It sold its mobile touch business in 2024 to focus on what it calls edge AI and the Internet of Things.
customers: Makers of PCs, smart home devices, cars, industrial equipment and consumer electronics, mostly in Asia.
money: Chips for PCs, docking stations, car displays and industrial devices.
Wireless and processor chips for smart home and connected devices.
Display and touch chips for phones, a shrinking line.
moat: Long relationships with PC and device makers, mixed-signal design expertise and a broad catalogue of connectivity chips. Its edge-AI processors are newer and must still win designs.
risks: Revenue fell from $1.74B in fiscal 2022 to $959M in fiscal 2024 when PC and consumer demand collapsed.
The fiscal 2026 net loss of $491M is far worse than cash flow suggests, and shows how charges can swamp reported earnings.
It competes with much larger chipmakers that can bundle more products together.
Most customers and manufacturing are in Asia, exposing it to trade restrictions and tariffs.
opportunities: Revenue has risen two years running, to $1.2B in fiscal 2026.
Operating cash flow stayed positive through the downturn, at about $149M in fiscal 2026.
Edge AI in PCs and devices could create a new growth market for its processors.
Analysts average a target of about $130, above the price.
watch: Design wins for its edge-AI and wireless chips, and whether revenue can approach its fiscal 2022 peak.
view: Synaptics is in the middle of a reinvention, and the numbers show it. Revenue fell by almost half after the 2022 PC boom ended, the company sold its mobile touch business, and it has been rebuilding around wireless and edge-AI chips. The fiscal 2026 net loss of $491 million looks alarming, but operating cash flow was positive at $149 million, so most of that loss was non-cash.

At $4.6 billion, the market pays about 20 times analysts’ forward earnings for a company whose revenue has recovered to $1.2 billion and whose old peak was $1.7 billion. That is a bet that the new product lines return it to growth. The design wins exist, but they are not yet large enough to show in margins.

This turns on whether Synaptics wins meaningful edge-AI and Wi-Fi designs in a market where Qualcomm and MediaTek are far larger. I would call it a show-me story: fairly priced for a recovery, not for a transformation, and I would want two or three quarters of rising gross margin before believing the new strategy works.
bull: Edge-AI and wireless design wins scale up, revenue returns toward its peak and margins expand.
bear: Larger chipmakers win the key designs and Synaptics remains a sub-scale supplier.
